environment.command: python -m pytest tests/unit tests/graph tests/integration/test_sync.py tests/integration/test_scenarios.py tests/integration/test_github.py -q --no-header -p no:cacheprovider

case.why: A link found in both versions is the normal case. If it is not reported valid, every update looks like a loss.
case.input: The same 3 links in both versions, over the same elements
case.expected: 3 valid links, none changed at either end; summary valid=3 and every other count 0

tests.description: A link both runs found, between unchanged elements, is valid and neither end changed.

case.feature: Change report / no longer found, neither end changed
case.why: When neither element changed and the link is gone, the cause is the classifier or a shifted top-k - not the artifacts. The report has to say so, because that is the case pinning exists for.
case.input: UC2 -> logout in the earlier version only; both elements unchanged and still present
case.expected: UC2 -> logout: no_longer_found, source_changed=false, target_changed=false

tests.description: A link that disappeared between two unchanged elements is no longer found, for no reason in the files.

case.why: An edited requirement is the most common reason a link moves. The report must name the source as the reason.
case.input: UC2's text edited between the versions, and UC2 -> logout no longer found
case.expected: UC2 -> logout: no_longer_found, source_changed=true, target_changed=false

tests.description: A link lost after its requirement was edited names the source as what changed.

case.why: Code changes under a requirement all the time. When that is what moved a link, the report must point at the code.
case.input: logout()'s body edited between the versions; UC2 -> logout still found
case.expected: UC2 -> logout: valid, source_changed=false, target_changed=true; the other two links valid with neither changed

tests.description: A link kept across an edit to its code says the target changed.

case.why: A link whose requirement or code was removed is broken: the one state that always needs a person to look. It must not be mistaken for the classifier changing its mind.
case.input: UC3 removed from the requirements (its id map entry says removed), and borrow() removed from the code in a second case
case.expected: UC3 -> borrow: broken with source_present=false and source_changed=true. In the second case: broken with target_present=false and target_changed=true

tests.description: A link with an end that no longer exists is broken, and says which end.
observed: requirement removed: {'state': 'broken', 'source_id': 'UC3', 'target_id': 'Loans::borrow()', 'source_present': False, 'target_present': True, 'source_changed': True, 'target_changed': False, 'confidence': 0.9, 'confidence_level': 'high', 'explanation': None}

code removed: {'state': 'broken', 'source_id': 'UC3', 'target_id': 'Loans::borrow()', 'source_present': True, 'target_present': False, 'source_changed': False, 'target_changed': True, 'confidence': 0.9, 'confidence_level': 'high', 'explanation': None}

case.why: A link only the later run found is what an update adds. Whether it came from new text or from the classifier matters for trusting it.
case.input: A new requirement UC4 linked to borrow() in the later version, and a new link UC1 -> logout between two unchanged elements
case.expected: UC4 -> borrow: new, source_changed=true (UC4 did not exist). UC1 -> logout: new, neither changed

tests.description: A link only the later run found is new, and says whether either end is new or edited.

case.why: Requirements with no link are the coverage gap a report exists to show. A requirement that was deleted is not a gap, and must not be listed as one.
case.input: Later version: UC2 has no link and still exists; UC3 was removed. The later run lists UC2 as unimplemented
case.expected: uncovered = ['UC2'] (UC3 is not listed); summary uncovered=1

tests.description: Sources with no link in the later version are listed; removed ones are not.

case.why: With sentence-level requirements, inserting a sentence renames the ones after it. Read without the id map, every later link would show as no longer found plus new.
case.input: Earlier: s0 -> login, s1 -> logout. A sentence inserted at 1, so s1 is now s2 (id map). Later: s0 -> login, s2 -> logout
case.expected: Both links valid, reported under the later identifiers (s0, s2), with neither end changed; no link new or no longer found

tests.description: A link whose element moved is the same link under its new identifier.

case.why: An analysis that was never updated has nothing to compare with. Its links must still be listed, as they stand.
case.input: No earlier run; a later run with 3 links and UC4 uncovered
case.expected: 3 links, all valid with neither end changed; uncovered ['UC4']

tests.description: With nothing to compare against, every link is reported as it stands.

case.feature: Change report / links per changed file
case.why: A changed file is worth looking at in proportion to the links it touches. Counting them per file is what lets the user go from a change to the links it affected.
case.input: Changed code files: Auth.java (modified) and security/Pay.java (renamed from Pay.java). Links: two into Auth.java (one whose target changed), one into security/Pay.java, one into Loans.java
case.expected: Auth.java: 2 links, 1 changed. security/Pay.java: 1 link, 1 changed. Loans.java is not a changed file and is not counted

tests.description: Each changed file says how many links touch it on its side, and how many say that end changed.

case.why: Every trace link is a parsed model reply. A reply read the wrong way is a wrong link shown to the user.
case.input: Well-formed replies: <trace>yes</trace>, <trace>NO</trace>, a <think> block saying yes followed by <trace>no</trace>, and a reply with an <explanation>
case.expected: yes -> linked, NO -> not linked, the <think> block is ignored, and the explanation text is returned

tests.description: A reply that follows the prompt's format is read from its tags, whatever else it says.
observed: simple: {'<trace>yes</trace>': True, '<trace>NO</trace>': False, '<think>yes, this could match</think>\n<trace>no</trace>': False, 'Reasoning: yes and no.\n<trace>no</trace>': False}
reasoning: {'<trace>yes</trace>': True, '<trace>NO</trace>': False, '<think>yes, this could match</think>\n<trace>no</trace>': False, 'Reasoning: yes and no.\n<trace>no</trace>': False}
reasoning with explanation: (True, 'The method checks the passphrase.')

case.why: Models sometimes omit the tag. Reading 'yes' inside another word turns a clear 'no' into a false trace link.
case.input: Replies with no <trace> tag: 'No. The eyes of the reader are not involved.' and 'No - that was removed yesterday.'
case.expected: Both read as not linked, by both classifiers

tests.description: A reply without the tag that plainly says no must not become a link.
observed: simple: 'No. The eyes of the reader are not involved.' -> not linked
simple: 'No - that was removed yesterday.' -> not linked
reasoning: 'No. The eyes of the reader are not involved.' -> not linked
reasoning: 'No - that was removed yesterday.' -> not linked

case.feature: Element diff / a sentence inserted in the middle
case.why: Sentences are named by position. One new sentence renames every sentence after it, which without the id map reads as every later link lost and found again, and offers pins to the wrong sentences.
case.input: UC1.txt with 3 sentences (login, logout, borrow); then the same file with a new sentence inserted between login and logout
case.expected: 1 sentence added (the new sentence_1); nothing removed or modified; logout and borrow moved from sentence_1 and sentence_2 to sentence_2 and sentence_3; login keeps its identifier

tests.description: An inserted sentence is the only addition; the sentences after it moved, not changed.

case.why: A removed sentence is what makes a link broken. The sentence after it takes over its position and identifier, so matching by identifier would wrongly say the removed sentence was edited.
case.input: UC1.txt with 3 sentences; then the same file without the middle one
case.expected: sentence_1 (logout) removed; borrow moved from sentence_2 to sentence_1; nothing added or modified; the removed identifier translates to nothing

tests.description: A removed sentence is reported removed, and the one that slid into its place is reported moved.

case.why: An edited sentence is the same requirement reworded. It must read as modified - the reason a link's source changed - not as one removed and one added.
case.input: UC1.txt with 3 sentences; then the same file with the login sentence reworded ('password' -> 'passphrase')
case.expected: 1 modified (sentence_0 -> sentence_0); nothing added, removed or moved. The whole-file element changed too, but only the compared sentences are listed

tests.description: A reworded sentence is modified in place.

case.why: Reordering changes no text. Both sentences must keep their links by moving with them, rather than each link pointing at the other sentence.
case.input: UC1.txt with login then logout; then logout then login
case.expected: Both moved (sentence_0 <-> sentence_1); nothing added, removed or modified

tests.description: Swapped sentences are two moves, and no edit.

case.feature: File diff / renamed with the same content
case.why: An uploaded folder has no rename list. A file moved without being edited must still be recognised by its content, or every link on it breaks.
case.input: Files {UC1.txt, UC2.txt}; then UC2.txt moved to archive/UC2.txt unchanged and UC1.txt edited. Then the elements of the moved file, read under both paths
case.expected: UC1.txt modified; UC2.txt renamed to archive/UC2.txt; nothing added or removed. Both sentences moved to the same identifier under the new path, and the id map takes the file itself there too

tests.description: A file whose content reappears under a new path is a rename, and its elements follow it.

case.why: Reformatting a file changes its bytes and its hash but not its meaning. It must not make a new version or be reported as an edit.
case.input: UC1.txt with 2 sentences; then the same text with extra spaces, a blank line and a trailing newline. And a Java file re-indented
case.expected: The file hashes differ, but no element is added, removed, modified or moved, and the change is not meaningful - for both files

tests.description: Only whitespace changed: the files differ, the elements do not.

case.feature: Element diff / UML components named by a counter
case.why: A component's identifier carries its position among the components. A component added at the front renumbers every other one, which must read as moves - not as every component replaced.
case.input: tests/data/model.uml (Authentication, Lending); then the same model with a new Catalogue component placed before them
case.expected: 1 component added (Catalogue, counter 0); Authentication moved from $0$ to $1$ and Lending from $1$ to $2; no component removed or modified

tests.description: A new component shifts the counters of the others; they are moved, not changed.

case.feature: Element diff / methods keep their names
case.why: A method is named by its signature, not its position. One rewritten beyond recognition is still the same method, and a method deleted while an unrelated one is added must not be called an edit.
case.input: Auth.java with login, logout, clear; then login's body rewritten, clear deleted, and a new method audit added after logout
case.expected: login modified (same identifier); clear removed; audit added; logout unchanged

tests.description: A rewritten method stays itself; a deleted one and a new one stay apart.
observed: shown to the user: {'added': ['Auth.java::Auth::audit(String event)'], 'removed': ['Auth.java::Auth::clear()'], 'modified': ['Auth.java::Auth::login(String name, String password)'], 'moved': []}

case.why: Pins are re-offered to the classifier by identifier. Untranslated, a pin made on the old sentence_1 is offered for whatever sentence now sits at position 1.
case.preconditions: The diff of U-29 (sentence inserted) on the source side and of U-30's kind (logout() removed) on the target side
case.input: Pins {sentence_0 -> login(), sentence_1 -> logout(), sentence_2 -> borrow()} translated through both id maps
case.expected: {sentence_0 -> login(), sentence_3 -> borrow()}: the logout pin is dropped because its target is gone, and borrow's source follows it to sentence_3

tests.description: Pins follow moved elements and are dropped when an end was removed.

case.why: The map is stored on a version and read back for the change report, which may span several versions. It must survive the round trip and chain correctly.
case.input: Version 2's map (sentence inserted at 1) and version 3's map (sentence_3 removed), stored as JSON-ready dicts, read back and composed
case.expected: Read back equal. Composed: sentence_1 -> sentence_2, sentence_2 -> gone (it became sentence_3, which version 3 removed), sentence_0 unchanged

tests.description: Maps read back from storage are the maps that were stored, and chain across versions.

case.feature: Id map / composed: insert, then remove at the same place
case.why: An identifier a later version removes names the element holding it after the earlier version, not the element that once had that name. Read the other way, a sentence that never went away is reported broken.
case.input: v2 inserts a sentence at s5, so the old s5 moves to s6. v3 removes the inserted sentence, so the old one moves back to s5
case.expected: v1's s5 translates to s5, and nothing is removed

tests.description: A sentence pushed down and back up again is still there under its old name.

case.why: Two swaps of the same pair put every element back where it was. Any leftover entry would send a link to the other element.
case.input: v2 swaps a and b; v3 swaps them back
case.expected: a translates to a and b to b; the composed map is empty

tests.description: Swapping twice returns every identifier to its element.

case.feature: Id map / composed: move, then remove
case.why: An element that moved and was then deleted is gone. Its links are broken, whatever name it had in between.
case.input: v2 moves s1 to s2; v3 removes s2
case.expected: v1's s1 translates to nothing

tests.description: An element removed after moving is removed.

case.feature: Id map / composed: removed, then another element moved onto the freed name
case.why: A freed identifier is soon taken by a neighbour. The removed element must stay removed, and the neighbour must not inherit its links.
case.input: v2 removes x; v3 moves y onto x
case.expected: x translates to nothing; y translates to x

tests.description: The element that takes a freed name is not the one that had it.

case.why: A report across several versions chains every map in between. The result must not depend on how the chain is grouped.
case.input: v2 inserts at s1 (s1->s2, s2->s3); v3 removes s3; v4 inserts at s0 (s0->s1, s1->s2, s2->s3). Composed left to right, and right to left
case.expected: s0->s1, s1->s3, s2 gone; both groupings give the same map

tests.description: Chaining three maps gives one answer, whichever pair is joined first.

case.why: A sentence that slid down because another was inserted is unchanged. Listing every one of them would bury the change that caused it; a sentence that went to another file is a real change.
case.input: UC1.txt: login, logout, borrow becomes: a new sentence, login, borrow - so login slides down one place. The logout sentence moved to UC2.txt
case.expected: Counts: 1 added, 2 moved. Listed: the added sentence, and the move to UC2.txt (old -> new); login, which only slid down, is not listed

tests.description: Elements that only changed position in their file are counted; a move to another file is listed.

case.why: A method renamed but otherwise kept is the same method. It must show as modified with its old and new name, and with a name a reader recognises.
case.input: Auth.java: login(String name) renamed to signIn(String name), body unchanged
case.expected: Listed once, as modified, old -> new: Auth.java::Auth::login(String name) -> Auth.java::Auth::signIn(String name), labelled 'Auth.signIn'

tests.description: A renamed method is one modified element, listed with its old and new identifier.

case.feature: Net change / a file renamed, then modified
case.why: Compared directly, a file renamed in one version and edited in a later one has a new path and new content, so nothing ties the two together. The renames the versions recorded have to.
case.input: v2 renames UC2.txt to archive/UC2.txt; v3 edits it; v4 renames it again to old/UC2.txt. The net file diff from v1 to v4, with and without the chained renames
case.expected: Chained renames: UC2.txt -> old/UC2.txt. With them, the file is renamed; without them, it reads as one removed and one added

tests.description: Renames recorded along the way tie a renamed and later edited file back to its old path.
observed: with them: renamed {'UC2.txt': 'old/UC2.txt'}; without: added ['old/UC2.txt'], removed ['UC2.txt']

case.feature: Element diff / a method removed beside one that was edited
case.why: When one method is removed and its neighbour is edited in the same commit, the edited one must stay itself. Pairing the removed method with it reports the wrong method as removed and sends its pinned links to the wrong place.
case.input: A class with getAll() and modify(Bean), whose bodies look alike. New version: getAll() removed, and one call inside modify(Bean) renamed
case.expected: getAll() removed; modify(Bean) modified and still mapped to itself; nothing added

tests.description: An edited method keeps its identity when a similar method next to it is removed.

case.why: A test run that touched the development database or its stored files would destroy real work.
case.input: The settings the application loaded under pytest
case.expected: Database is 'tracerag_test', not the one in .env; storage and the working folder are under tests/.work

tests.description: The application under test is pointed at the test database and a scratch storage folder.
observed: database in use: tracerag_test; database in .env: tracerag

case.why: Guarantees no test can reach Ollama, Groq, GitHub or HuggingFace, so results never depend on them.
case.input: Open a socket to api.github.com:443 and to localhost:11434 (Ollama)
case.expected: Both refused with OSError before any connection is made

tests.description: A connection that would leave the machine, or reach Ollama, is refused.
observed: api.github.com:443 -> Network access is blocked in tests: api.github.com:443
localhost:11434 -> Network access is blocked in tests: localhost:11434

case.why: Every other test's result depends on the fakes giving the same answer on every run.
case.input: Embed the same text twice; classify a related pair and an unrelated pair
case.expected: Identical vectors; related pair linked, unrelated pair not; shared-word texts closer than unrelated ones

tests.description: The fake embedder and classifier give the same answer every time.

case.why: This value becomes a browser redirect after sign-in. If it can name another site, a link that looks like ours lands on an attacker's.
case.input: '/app/history?project=4', 'https://evil.com', '//evil.com', '/\\evil.com', 'app/profile', '' and None
case.expected: Only the first is kept; every other value becomes the default '/app/profile'

tests.description: Only a path inside the app is accepted as somewhere to send the browser back to.

case.why: The state says whose account a GitHub token gets attached to. A forged or reused one would attach it to someone else.
case.input: A valid state; one with a character changed; one signed for another purpose; an expired one; an ordinary login token used as state
case.expected: The valid one returns (user id, return path); the other four are refused with a GitHubError

tests.description: A state token is accepted only if it is ours, unexpired and made for this handshake.
observed: tampered -> That sign-in link is not valid.
wrong purpose -> That sign-in link is not valid.
expired -> That sign-in link has expired. Try connecting again.
login token -> That sign-in link is not valid.

case.why: A repository tarball is unpacked onto the server. Entries with '..' or symlinks are how an archive escapes its folder.
case.input: A tar.gz shaped like GitHub's: 'repo-abc/src/A.java', 'repo-abc/../../evil.java', a symlink, and a file with no folder
case.expected: Only src/A.java is written, without the 'repo-abc' wrapper folder; nothing outside the destination

tests.description: Only plain files inside the repository are unpacked, with GitHub's wrapper folder dropped.

case.why: Users paste whatever GitHub shows them. Each form must resolve to the same repository, and junk must be refused before any request.
case.input: 'owner/repo', 'https://github.com/owner/repo', 'github.com/owner/repo.git', 'git@github.com:owner/repo.git', a URL with a trailing slash and a /tree/main suffix; then 'not a repository!!' and ''
case.expected: Every valid form -> 'owner/repo'; the two invalid values raise GitHubError

tests.description: Every way GitHub writes a repository's address is understood; anything else is refused.
observed: 'not a repository!!' -> 'not a repository!!' does not look like a GitHub repository. Paste its URL, or write it as owner/name.
'' -> '' does not look like a GitHub repository. Paste its URL, or write it as owner/name.

case.why: GitHub tokens are stored in the database. They must not be readable there, and a changed key must fail loudly, not return garbage.
case.input: Encrypt 'ghp_exampletoken', decrypt it, then decrypt it again after the secret key has changed
case.expected: The stored value does not contain the token; decrypting returns it; with another key, SecretError

tests.description: A stored token is unreadable without the key, and says so when the key is wrong.
observed: with a different key: A stored access token could not be read. This happens when secret_key changes; the connection has to be made again.

case.why: Pinned links are matched by identifier across runs. This mismatch already broke pinning twice, silently.
case.input: Real identifiers from DocumentProvider (relative) and CodeProvider (absolute) over the same workspace
case.expected: Both reduce to workspace-relative paths with '/' separators; the '::member' part is unchanged

tests.description: The two providers name elements differently; the stored form must be the same for both.
observed: stored form of the document: UC1.txt
stored form of the method: Auth.java::Auth::login(String name, String passphrase)

case.why: A root that is only a name-prefix of another folder must not be stripped, or two files would get one identifier.
case.input: A nested file, a file in a sibling folder whose name starts with the root's name, and a path outside every root
case.expected: Nested -> 'pkg/sub/A.java'; sibling and outside paths returned exactly as given

tests.description: A path is shortened only when it is really inside a workspace root.

case.why: The graph and the caches decide 'unchanged' by this hash; a formatter run must not look like a rewrite.
case.input: A method, the same method with trailing spaces and blank lines added, and the method with one word changed
case.expected: First two hashes equal; the third different

tests.description: Whitespace a reader would not notice does not change what the content is.

case.why: A UML component's identifier is a counter and an XMI id, which means nothing to a reader. Every screen and export shows the name this returns, so it has to name each element once and unambiguously.
case.input: A component 'Authentication'; two components called 'Lending' in two model files; a component with no name; a sentence and a method
case.expected: 'Authentication'; 'Lending (a.uml)' and 'Lending (b.uml)'; the nameless component and the sentence and method keep their identifiers. model_name gives a name only at component level

tests.description: Components are named by their model; duplicates get their file; everything else keeps its id.

case.why: Top-k is a fixed budget. Without pinning, a link vanishes when retrieval stops surfacing it, though nothing rejected it.
case.preconditions: A first run with top-k 10 found both links of one requirement
case.input: The same files run again with top-k 1, once without pins and once with the first run's links as pins
case.expected: Without pins: 1 link (one lost). With pins: both links kept

tests.description: A link retrieval no longer surfaces is offered to the classifier again and kept.

case.why: Checks load, split, embed, retrieve, classify and aggregate fit together before any database or API is involved.
case.input: tests/data: 4 use cases against 2 Java files (5 methods), whole documents -> methods, top-k 10
case.expected: UC1->login, UC2->logout, UC3->borrow; UC4 unimplemented; with expansion depth 1, a strong link to logout() also reaches clear(), which it calls

tests.description: The whole pipeline, on a corpus where the right answer is known.

case.why: Pins in the wrong form match nothing and look exactly like having nothing to carry over; the warning is the only sign.
case.preconditions: A first run with top-k 10 found both links of one requirement
case.input: Top-k 1 with pins keyed by absolute paths instead of the stored relative form
case.expected: Nothing carried over (1 link), and a warning that no pinned identifier matched

tests.description: Pins that do not match this run's identifiers are reported, not silently ignored.
observed: warning: None of the 1 pinned source identifier(s) match this run's elements, so no link can be carried over. They are probably stored in a different form than the run produces.

case.why: Methods are what links are found on. Wrong identifiers or parents break rolling a link up to its class or file.
case.input: tests/data/code/Auth.java: one class with login, logout and clear
case.expected: 1 file and 1 class (not compared), 3 methods (compared); each method's parent is the class, the class's parent is the file

tests.description: A Java file is split into a file, its class, and one element per method.
observed: ['code/Auth.java [file, compare=False]', 'code/Auth.java::Auth [class, compare=False]', 'code/Auth.java::Auth::login(String name, String passphrase) [function, compare=True]', 'code/Auth.java::Auth::logout() [function, compare=True]', 'code/Auth.java::Auth::clear() [function, compare=True]']

case.why: Users choose to see links per file. Two methods of one file must become one link, not two, and not a link on the wrong file.
case.input: Three method-level results for one requirement: A.m1 (0.9), A.m2 (0.6) and B.m1 (0.5); target level FILE
case.expected: Two links: req -> A.java at 0.9 and req -> B.java at 0.5; with no target level, all three stay as they are

tests.description: Links are reported on the ancestor at the requested level, one per pair.

case.why: These decide what a requirement element is. One file must be one element, or one per sentence, with stable identifiers.
case.input: tests/data/arch.txt (two sentences) through ArtifactPreprocessor and SentencePreprocessor
case.expected: Whole document: 1 compared element. Sentences: the document (not compared) plus 2 compared sentences named '::sentence_0' and '::sentence_1'

tests.description: A document is read as one element, or as one element per sentence under it.

case.why: The architecture diagram and the links both come from this: a component's provided and required interfaces must be right.
case.input: tests/data/model.uml: Authentication provides IAuth; Lending provides ILending and uses IAuth
case.expected: 2 compared components with those interfaces and their operations in the text; 2 interfaces, not compared

tests.description: A UML model is split into components, each knowing what it provides and requires.

case.why: Expansion multiplies links. It must stop at the depth asked for and must not grow weak links into more weak links.
case.input: Call chain a -> b -> c. A strong link (0.9) and a weak link (0.3) to a, expanded at depth 1 and depth 2
case.expected: Depth 1: strong link reaches b only. Depth 2: reaches b and c with decayed confidence. The weak link is never expanded

tests.description: Links follow call edges up to the depth given, losing confidence with each step.

case.why: Each side's elements live in a collection. If both sides shared one, an element would be offered as a candidate for itself.
case.input: requirements -> code, and requirements -> requirements
case.expected: Two different collection names in both cases, each named after its kind

tests.description: The two sides of a run never share a collection, even when they hold the same kind.

case.feature: Preprocessing / functions that share a name
case.why: An identifier names exactly one element. Two functions with one name and one parameter list in a file - in different scopes, or in minified code - got the same identifier, and the vector index refused the whole run.
case.input: A JavaScript file with Plugin(option) defined twice, in two scopes, and one function defined once; then a full pipeline run with that file among the code
case.expected: Every identifier is unique: the first keeps its name, the second ends '#2', and the function defined once is unchanged. The pipeline run finishes

tests.description: A second function with the same name and parameters is numbered instead of repeating an identifier.
observed: pipeline run finished with 3 links; app.js functions indexed: 3

case.why: Expansion only happens for code. Recording it for other kinds would claim an expansion that never happened.
case.input: Depth 2 with target kind code, architecture, architecture_document, requirements, and unknown (None)
case.expected: code -> 2; the other three kinds -> 0; unknown -> 2 (left as given)

tests.description: Dependency expansion is recorded as 0 unless the target is code.

case.why: A zip entry named '../x' is the classic way an upload writes outside its folder and overwrites server files.
case.input: A zip with entries 'src/A.java', '../evil.java', '../../deep/evil.java' and '/abs.java'
case.expected: All four files end up inside the destination; nothing is written outside it; the archive is removed

tests.description: Entries that try to climb out of the destination are kept inside it.

case.why: File paths come from the browser. One that survives as '../' or as an absolute path can write anywhere on the server.
case.input: 'a/b.txt', '../../etc/passwd', '/etc/passwd', 'C:\\Windows\\x.txt', 'a\\..\\b', './a/./b', '  /x//y ', 'we!rd$name.java', ''
case.expected: Every result is relative, has no '..' part, and resolves inside the destination; '' becomes 'file'

tests.description: Whatever path is supplied, the result stays inside the folder it is written to.

case.why: The total limit is what stops one request from filling the disk with many files that are each under the per-file limit.
case.input: A budget of 10 bytes: consume 6, then 4, then 1 more
case.expected: The first two are accepted; the third raises UploadTooLarge naming the file

tests.description: Bytes are counted across the whole request, and the limit is exact.

case.input: Update the requirements with an edited UC1, with a classifier that answers one question and then raises
case.expected: The job fails with the classifier's error. The analysis still has only version 1 with its one run and its 3 links; its requirements fingerprint is unchanged; the report still answers; no working folder is left

tests.description: A classifier that dies in the middle of an update leaves the analysis exactly as it was.
observed: job: failed - the classifier stopped answering
links of the saved run: 3; report {'valid': 3, 'no_longer_found': 0, 'broken': 0, 'new': 0, 'uncovered': 1}
fingerprint unchanged: True; new working folders: []

case.feature: Update / bad files handed over for a side
case.why: The Update dialog takes files from the user's disk. A bad set must be refused before anything runs, never become a version, and never leave a half-written set on the server.
case.preconditions: A saved requirements->code analysis at version 1; the per-file limit lowered to 1,000 bytes
case.input: Stage for an update: no files; a .md file for the requirements; a file named .zip that is not a zip, for the code; an oversized requirements file
case.expected: 400, 400, 400 and 413, each with a message. The analysis still has 1 version and no working folder is left

tests.description: Bad files for an update are refused, make no version and leave nothing behind.
observed: no files: 400 - Choose at least one file.
wrong extension: 400 - 'notes.md' is not a supported requirements file. Accepted: .docx, .pdf, .txt.
not a zip: 400 - '__archive_0.zip' is not a valid .zip archive.
oversized file: 413 - 'UC1.txt' exceeds the 0 MB per-file limit.

case.feature: Access control / the endpoints I-20 does not reach
case.why: I-20 covers most endpoints. The line diff, the analysis itself and the update endpoints with no login at all are the ones it leaves out, and each of them reads or changes another user's analysis.
case.preconditions: User A owns an analysis at version 2 (UC1 edited). User B is a different signed-in user
case.input: As B: the analysis, its line diff, its delete. With no login: the analysis, report, line diff, sides, update status, staging, update, GitHub side, re-run, run delete and analysis delete
case.expected: Every request by B gets 404; every anonymous request gets 401. A's analysis still has 2 versions and its sides afterwards

tests.description: The line diff, the analysis itself and every update endpoint refuse other users and anonymous callers.

case.feature: Data integrity / versions, runs and stored files
case.why: Every screen trusts three things: a version always has a run, every file a version lists can be read back, and deleting a run never takes files another version still needs.
case.preconditions: An analysis taken through four versions as in I-49, with version 4 re-run once so it holds two runs
case.input: Check every version and file row of the analysis; delete one of version 4's runs and collect garbage with the grace period switched off; check again, and read every version's files back
case.expected: Before and after the delete: every version has at least one run, and every file row's blob is in the store. After the delete version 4 keeps one run, none of the analysis's blobs is retired, and every artifact still downloads

tests.description: No version without a run, no file row without its blob, and a deleted run takes no shared files.
observed: before delete: versions without a run [], rows without a blob []
delete run: 204; blobs retired by garbage collection: 0
after delete: versions without a run [], rows without a blob []; artifact downloads: [200]

case.why: UML components are named by a counter, so a component added in front renumbers every one after it. An update that changes one component must not break the links of the others, and must still show them by name.
case.preconditions: A saved requirements -> architecture model analysis at component level over model.uml (Authentication, Lending)
case.input: Update the model with a new component 'Audit' inserted before Authentication, so both existing components get a new counter; read the report
case.expected: Version 2. Every link of version 1 is valid, none broken or no longer found. Every link in the report and in version 2's run carries a component name, never a raw '$' id

tests.description: Inserting one UML component renumbers the others but keeps their links, shown by name.
observed: update: Version 2: target side updated, 3 trace links.; elements {'added': ['model.uml$0$_audit'], 'removed': [], 'modified': [], 'moved': [{'old': 'model.uml$0$_auth', 'new': 'model.uml$1$_auth'}, {'old': 'model.uml$1$_lend', 'new': 'model.uml$2$_lend'}]}

case.why: A commit that only reformats files changes the commit id but not the code. It must make no version, and the side must stop showing as changed afterwards, or the Update button nags forever.
case.preconditions: A saved requirements->code analysis whose code side was taken from the repository at commit-1 (same files as stored)
case.input: Push commit-2 with the same code re-indented and with trailing blank lines; read the status, update, read the status again; then push commit-3 with a real change
case.expected: Before the update: changed, commit-1 -> commit-2. The update makes no version ('No meaningful change'). Afterwards: not changed, at commit-2. Commit-3 is then detected as changed again

tests.description: A reformatting commit makes no version and is then no longer reported as new.
observed: update: 'No meaningful change: 2 file(s) differ, but no element the analysis compares changed. No new version was made.'
status after the update: (False, 'commit-2', 'commit-2'); after a real change: (True, 'commit-2', 'commit-3')

case.feature: Deleting a run / the only run of a version
case.why: A version without a run has no links, so the change report has nothing to compare it by. Its last run must not be deletable.
case.preconditions: A saved analysis at v1 with one run
case.input: DELETE that run
case.expected: 409 'This is the only run of this version.'; the run is still there and v1 still has 1 run

tests.description: Deleting a version's last run is refused.
observed: delete: 409 - This is the only run of this version.; run afterwards: 200; versions [(1, 1)]

case.feature: Deleting a run / one of several
case.why: The refusal must only stop the last run; clearing out a re-run stays routine.
case.preconditions: A saved analysis at v1 with a run and a re-run
case.input: DELETE the re-run; then DELETE the remaining run
case.expected: 204, and v1 keeps 1 run; then 409 for the remaining run

tests.description: A version with two runs can lose one of them, not both.
observed: delete the re-run: 204; versions [(1, 1)]; delete the last run: 409

case.feature: Change report / an earlier version with no run
case.why: Versions left without a run by an older delete still exist. Comparing against one must not fail and hide the later version's links.
case.preconditions: An analysis at v2 (UC1 edited) whose v1 run was deleted before deleting the last run was refused
case.input: Read the report for 1 -> 2; then remove v2's run as well and read 1 -> 2 again
case.expected: 1 -> 2: 200, no_run_version 1, v2's 3 links returned, the net change of the files still there. With v2's run gone too: 200, no_run_version 2, no links

tests.description: A run-less earlier version gives the later version's links, uncompared, instead of an error.
observed: with v2's run gone too: no_run_version 2; links 0

case.feature: Change report / which earlier version is chosen
case.why: The Trace Links page opens on the default comparison. It must compare against the nearest version that has links, not a run-less one.
case.preconditions: An analysis at v3 (UC1 edited in v2, again in v3) whose v2 run was deleted; and one at v2 whose v1 run was deleted
case.input: Read the default report of each
case.expected: First: 1 -> 3, compared (no_run_version none). Second: 1 -> 2 with no_run_version 1 and v2's links, since no earlier version has a run

tests.description: By default the report compares against the nearest earlier version with a run.
observed: v3 with a run-less v2: 1 -> 3, no_run_version None, {'valid': 3, 'no_longer_found': 0, 'broken': 0, 'new': 0, 'uncovered': 1}
v2 with a run-less v1: 1 -> 2, no_run_version 1, links 3

case.feature: GitHub update / fetch, version and follow renames

Afterwards the side reports no change

case.why: The callback attaches a GitHub token to a user and then redirects the browser. Both the stored token and the redirect target have to be safe.
case.preconditions: GitHub's token exchange is replaced by a fake that returns a token and the login 'octocat'
case.input: Start OAuth from /app/history, follow the callback; then a callback with a forged state; then start with return_to=//evil.example
case.expected: The browser returns to /app/history with github=connected. The token is stored encrypted and the connection reads connected as octocat. A forged state redirects to the profile page with an error. An outside return address is replaced by the profile page

tests.description: Connecting GitHub stores the token encrypted and only ever sends the browser back into the app.
observed: stored token is plain text: False; decrypts to the token: True

case.feature: GitHub connection / a credential GitHub has rejected
case.why: A dead token left in place makes the app say 'connected' while every sync fails. The app must notice, clear it, and offer to reconnect.
case.preconditions: A user with a connected GitHub account and an analysis whose code side is a GitHub repository
case.input: GitHub starts rejecting the token. Read the update status, then the connection
case.expected: The code side reports an error with needs_reconnect=true and is not marked changed. The stored account token is cleared, and the connection reads not connected

tests.description: When GitHub rejects the stored token, the app drops it and says the account must be reconnected.
observed: code side status: changed=False, needs_reconnect=True, error=GitHub rejected the access token.

case.why: The Connect dialog offers 'Reconnect GitHub' instead of the form when the account connection has died. That only works if the connection check says so.
case.preconditions: A user who connected their GitHub account
case.input: GitHub starts rejecting the token. Read the connection twice
case.expected: First read: not connected, needs_reconnect=true, and the dead token is cleared. Second read: not connected, needs_reconnect=false - there is nothing stored left to reject

tests.description: The connection check reports a token GitHub has just rejected as needing a reconnect.
observed: first read: {'connected': False, 'login': None, 'configured': True, 'needs_reconnect': True}
second read: {'connected': False, 'login': None, 'configured': True, 'needs_reconnect': False}

case.feature: GitHub side / whose credential a fetch uses
case.why: With the account connected, a code side is taken from GitHub without a token of its own, and every fetch must use the account connection. A side given its own token on purpose must keep using that one.
case.preconditions: A user who connected their GitHub account (token gho_token_for_abc), with two saved analyses
case.input: Analysis A: take the code side from the repository with no token, and update it. Analysis B: take it with its own token 'side-token', and update it
case.expected: A's side stores no token (has_token=false) and its fetch used the account token. B's side stores its token (has_token=true) and its fetch used 'side-token'

tests.description: A side without a token is fetched with the account connection; a side with one uses its own.
observed: account side: has_token=False; own-token side: has_token=True
